subject: Biology

nodes.text: the cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all living things
the cell membrane surrounds the cell and controls what materials move in and out
the nucleus contains the DNA and controls the cell's activities
the cytoplasm is the jelly-like fluid where the organelles sit and reactions happen
mitochondria release energy through respiration and are called the powerhouse of the cell
plant cells also have a rigid cell wall, chloroplasts for photosynthesis, and a large vacuole
eukaryotic cells keep their DNA inside a nucleus while prokaryotic cells have no true nucleus

textbookPhrasings: The cell is the basic structural and functional unit of life, and all living organisms are composed of cells.
The nucleus is the control centre of the cell and contains the genetic material.
Plant cells differ from animal cells in having a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large central vacuole.
referenceFacts: The cell is the basic unit of life
The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell
The nucleus contains DNA and controls the cell
Plant cells have a cell wall and chloroplasts
Eukaryotic cells have a nucleus while prokaryotic cells do not

whyQuestions.q: Why do plant cells have a cell wall but animal cells do not?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: the rigid cell wall gives plant cells support and shape since they have no skeleton

whyQuestions.q: Why is the nucleus often called the control centre of the cell?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: it holds the DNA, the instructions that direct the cell's activities

whyQuestions.q: Why can a cell die if its membrane is badly damaged?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: the membrane controls what goes in and out, so damage lets harmful substances in and essentials leak out

misconceptions: Only animals are made of cells, not plants
The cell wall and cell membrane are the same thing
The cytoplasm is empty space inside the cell
